_doc: A WORN YARD (T-3339). The ground round kinzie_house_1812, kinzie_bake_house_1812, kinzie_dairy_1812, kinzie_lodging_house_1812, kinzie_stable_1812 as trodden earth feathered into the sward by renderers/web/js/yards.js. NOT ONE COORDINATE HERE IS AUTHORED - the ring is the convex hull of the buildings' committed footprints pushed out 3.5 m, written by tools/generate_worn_ground_1812.py and re-derived byte for byte by tools/check.sh. It draws no fence (`runs: []`). docs/LIBERTIES.md L-t3339-worn-ground-1812.
name: Worn ground: The Kinzie house's working yard behind it
coordinates: Local East-North-Up metres from data/datum.json's origin.

existence.note: The Kinzie house's working yard behind it: stable, dairy, bake house and the men's lodging house. Its front keeps Wau-Bun's 'broad green space' to the river. That the ground round a used building was worn bare in patches is this project's reading; no source describes it. docs/LIBERTIES.md L-t3339-worn-ground-1812.

runs_note: EMPTY, AND DELIBERATELY: worn ground round a building, not a fenced yard.

ground.note: worn_earth where stock stood and wheels turned; trodden_earth at a dooryard.
ground.wear_note: How bare the ground is, 0..1: the share of the treatment drawn and of the sward taken away. Sized by the traffic the building drew.

assertions.claim: the yard lies on no garden or field footprint
no corner of the yard lies on water
